# Product-cone energy and pointed exposed-face blow-up

This is a complete ordinary product-model theorem. It identifies the
exact codimension-k coefficient, proves that the normal optimization
is attained, and gives the lower-dimensional escort marginal. It also
proves a bounded convex-body limit for truncated product cones. Section7
extends this to actual exposed faces with a CLOSED POINTED projected
cone, with full local and tail controls. No claim covers faces lacking
that hypothesis, and no mixed depth conclusion is asserted.

The compact-body energy, affine covariance, strict parameter minimization
and escort identities are from
`candidate 5811f0ad1132ce56`.
The codimension-one limit is in
`candidate 1389446c1fac70ac`.

## 1. Product geometry and the normal-cone constant

Let 1<=k<=d, put m=d-k, and use orthogonal coordinates(z,q) in
R^m times R^k. Let F be a convex body in R^m and x in int F. When m=0,
F is one point, E_F=1 and its measure is counting measure. Let Q be a
closed, pointed, full-dimensional convex cone in R^k, and fix v in int Q.
Write Q*={b:b.q>=0 for all q in Q}. For b in int Q* define

    J_Q(b)=int_Q exp(-b.q)dq,
    J_*(v)=min{J_Q(n):n in int Q*, n.v=1}.               (1)

This minimum is finite and uniquely attained at a vector n_v. In
particular it is an actual geometric quantity of the normal cone and
the marked approach vector, not an arbitrary measure relaxation.

Proof of attainment: pointedness supplies a vector strictly positive
on the compact set Q cap S^(k-1), hence int Q* is nonempty. One elementary
way to see this is that zero cannot belong to the convex hull of those
unit cone vectors: a positive combination summing to zero would give
a line in Q. The closest point of their compact convex hull to zero
therefore supplies a strictly positive linear functional.
For b in int Q*, b.q>=c|q| on Q for some c>0, so J_Q(b) is finite.
On the normalized closed dual slice n in Q*, n.v=1, an interior ball
v+rB subset Q gives1=n.v>=r|n|. Thus this slice is compact.

If n is on the boundary of Q*, some nonzero w in Q has n.w=0.
Choose a ball inside Q. Its translates by sufficiently separated
positive multiples of w are disjoint balls still inside Q, all with
the same exponential integral. Consequently J_Q(n)=infinity. Fatou
then shows J_Q tends to infinity along any interior normalized sequence
approaching such a boundary point. This proves attained interior
minimization. The Hessian

    Hess J_Q(b)=int_Q qq^T exp(-b.q)dq

is positive definite, so the restriction to n.v=1 is strictly convex
and its minimizer is unique. Differentiation is justified by uniform
exponential domination on compact subsets of int Q*.

Homogeneity is J_Q(t b)=t^(-k)J_Q(b), t>0. The constrained stationarity
and Euler identity give the further exact identity

    [int_Q q exp(-n_v.q)dq]/J_Q(n_v)=k v.               (2)

Indeed the left side is a scalar multiple of v by stationarity, and
its dot product with n_v equals k. This is an ordinary exponential
law on the actual cone.

## 2. Exact energy of the infinite product model

Define the projective integral on F times Q at(x,v) by the same
positive affine-denominator formula as for compact bodies, allowing
the integral to be infinite. Its infimum is finite and attained, and
has the exact value

 E_(F times Q)(x,v)=C_(d,k)(Q,v) E_F(x),

 C_(d,k)(Q,v)= [m!/d!] [(d+1)^(d+1)
                      /(k^k(m+1)^(m+1))] J_*(v).       (3)

This is proved directly; it does not apply a compact-body existence
claim to an unbounded set.

Write a candidate denominator as

    L(z,q)=1+c.(z-x)+b.(q-v).

For a finite positive integral one must have b in int Q* and
1-b.v+c.(z-x)>0 on F. A negative value b.w on a cone ray violates
positivity. A zero value on a nonzero ray gives the infinite-cylinder
argument from Section1, now for the inverse-power integrand. Thus
boundary b in Q* cannot have finite objective. In particular
beta=b.v lies in(0,1).

For any r>k and positive h, Tonelli and the elementary gamma integral
prove

 int_Q(h+b.q)^(-r)dq
       =[Gamma(r-k)/Gamma(r)] J_Q(b) h^(-(r-k)).         (4)

Indeed insert a Laplace integral for the inverse power and use
int_Q exp(-t b.q)dq=t^(-k)J_Q(b). With r=d+1, integration first in q
gives

 int_(F times Q) L^(-d-1)
  =[m!/d!] J_Q(b) int_F[1-beta+c.(z-x)]^(-m-1)dz
  >=[m!/d!] J_Q(b)(1-beta)^(-m-1)E_F(x).                (5)

Equality holds exactly when c=(1-beta)a_F, where a_F is the actual
optimal facet/body parameter (empty if m=0). Put n=b/beta, so n.v=1.
Then J_Q(b)=beta^(-k)J_Q(n). Minimizing(5) reduces to minimizing
J_Q(n) and maximizing beta^k(1-beta)^(m+1). The latter has the unique
maximizer beta=k/(d+1). Hence the unique product-model parameters are

    b_*=[k/(d+1)] n_v,
    c_*=[(m+1)/(d+1)] a_F,                             (6)

and(3) follows. All positivity requirements are satisfied there.

By normal dilation of this SAME product cone,

    E_(F times Q)(x,delta v)
          =delta^k C_(d,k)(Q,v) E_F(x)                 (7)

for every delta>0. No asymptotic is needed for the infinite model.

## 3. A bounded actual convex-body blow-up theorem

Fix ell in int Q* and H>0, and take the COMPACT convex body

    K=F times Q_H,
    Q_H={q in Q:ell.q<=H}.                             (8)

For all sufficiently small delta, (x,delta v) is an interior point.
Then

    E_K(x,delta v)/delta^k
                    ->C_(d,k)(Q,v)E_F(x).              (9)

Moreover if the original minimizing parameter is(c_delta,beta_delta),
then

    c_delta -> c_*,   delta beta_delta -> b_*.           (10)

Proof: normal dilation by1/delta gives the nested bodies
F times Q_(H/delta), with common source(x,v), exhausting F times Q.
They eventually contain a fixed full-dimensional ball about that source.
Thus their actual minimizing parameters are uniformly bounded. Testing
the product-model optimum gives a uniform finite upper bound, namely
its full product-model integral. Their optimal denominators have the
compact-body floor1/(d+1), proved in the audited energy-supergradient
source. Every parameter subsequential limit therefore has that floor
on the entire limiting product, by exhaustion.

Fatou along that subsequence bounds the limiting product integral by
the limit inferior of the attained compact-body energies. It is finite
by the preceding uniform test. Consequently its normal parameter is
in int Q*, by the infinite-cylinder argument, and it is a valid
finite product-model parameter. Its integral is at least(3). Conversely
each compact-body energy is at most the product-model test integral,
which tends increasingly to(3). These two bounds prove(9) after the
Jacobian factor delta^k. Uniqueness in Section2 identifies every
parameter cluster point, proving(10).

This is an actual compact positive-body theorem. Section7 separately
proves the local tangential geometry and uniform tail control needed
for a specified nonproduct exposed-face extension.

## 4. Exact lower-dimensional escort marginal

Put N=d+1 and write the optimal product denominator as

    L_*(z,q)=[(m+1)/N] L_F(z)+b_*.q,
    L_F(z)=1+a_F.(z-x).

The product escort is the probability density

    rho_*(z,q)=L_*(z,q)^(-d-2)
                         /[C_(d,k)(Q,v)E_F(x)]         (11)

on F times Q. In particular its normalization is the same energy
constant as the projective volume, just as in the compact case.
To check this and its exact tangential marginal, apply(4) with r=d+2.
Relative to the energy integration factor in(5), its gamma factor is
(m+1)/(d+1), exactly canceled by the additional power of
(1-beta_*)=(m+1)/(d+1). Hence

    int_Q rho_*(z,q)dq=L_F(z)^(-m-2)/E_F(x).             (12)

This is the ordinary m-dimensional escort on F, including the point
convention when m=0.

There is an exact normal conditional mean as well. Differentiating
the cone Laplace integral, or inserting it in the same Tonelli formula,
gives for h>0

 E[q under density proportional to(h+b.q)^(-d-2)]
             =[-grad log J_Q(b)] h/(m+1).

By(2), homogeneity and(6), -grad log J_Q(b_*)=N v.
Taking h=(m+1)L_F(z)/N therefore gives

    E[q|z]=L_F(z)v.                                    (13)

The facet escort expectation of L_F is1, so the full mean is(x,v).

For the bounded bodies(8), their NORMAL-DILATED escort densities converge
to(11) in L1 and in first moments. Indeed(10) places their normal
parameters in a compact subset of int Q*, so at large |q| the
denominators dominate c|q| uniformly on the cone; at bounded |q| the
optimal floor1/(d+1) applies on the actual bodies. The tangent variables
stay in compact F and the energies tend to a positive constant. A
uniform multiple of(1+|q|)^(-d-2) dominates the densities. This and its
first-moment bound are integrable in k dimensions since d>=k. Exhaustion
and parameter convergence give the claimed dominated convergence.
Undoing the dilation, the original escort laws converge weakly onto
F times{0}, with precisely the lower-dimensional escort(12).

## 5. Simplicial cones: exact consistency of facet constants

For Q=R_+^k and v with all coordinates positive,

    J_Q(n)=product_(j=1)^k n_j^(-1),
    n_v,j=1/(k v_j),  J_*(v)=k^k product_j v_j.

Therefore(3) simplifies to

 C_(d,k)(R_+^k,v)
   =[m!/d!] [(d+1)^(d+1)/(m+1)^(m+1)] product_j v_j
   =[product_(r=m+1)^d ((r+1)/r)^(r+1)] product_j v_j. (14)

The second equality is an exact telescoping product. Thus the
simultaneous orthant coefficient is EXACTLY the product of the
successive facet coefficients, multiplied by the k normal approach
coordinates. The escort marginal recursion is also consistent,
because every reduction leaves precisely the escort of the remaining
tangential body.

For a simplicial cone Q=G R_+^k with invertible G, put w=G^(-1)v>0.
Normal change of variables gives

    J_*(v)=|det G| k^k product_j w_j.                    (15)

Hence(14) acquires the expected Jacobian |det G| and the actual
simplicial coordinates w. This statement tracks volume normalization;
it does not identify oblique coordinate distances with Euclidean
facet distances without their determinant factor.

## 6. A nonsimplicial cone retains genuine path geometry

The general constant is NOT a universal codimension factor times the
product of any arbitrarily chosen k facet distances. An exact polyhedral
calibration is the three-dimensional square cone

    Q={ (X,Y,T):T>=|X|, T>=|Y| }.

For n=(b,0,a), a>|b|, direct integration over each square section gives

    J_Q(b,0,a)=8a/(a^2-b^2)^2.                         (16)

For v_s=(s,0,1), |s|<1, symmetry in Y and unique minimization force
the second normal coefficient to be0. Set t=b/a, so the constraint
n.v_s=1 gives a=1/(1+s t), and

    J_*(v_s)=min_(-1<t<1) 8(1+s t)^3/(1-t^2)^2.         (17)

For s>0 its stationary equation is s t^2+4t+3s=0. The unique root
in(-1,1) is the unique minimizer, by Section1. At s=0 it is t=0 and
J_*(v_0)=8. At s=8/13 it is t=-1/2, yielding exactly

    J_*(v_(8/13))=10368/2197,
    J_*(v_(8/13))/J_*(v_0)=1296/2197.                  (18)

The four facet distances, with the same normalizations at both points,
have ratios1-s,1+s,1,1. Products from ANY three of the four facets
therefore have ratios1-s^2,1-s,or1+s. At s=8/13 these are respectively
1365/2197,845/2197,and3549/2197, all different from(18).
Thus even this bounded product-cone model retains a nontrivial normal
optimization not encoded by one such facet-distance product. The ratio
is independent of the tangential F and cancels every dimensional
prefactor in(3).

Equations(14)--(15) prove consistent composition along the simplicial
product model. Equations(16)--(18) demonstrate why a general simultaneous
codimension limit must retain the normal cone and approach vector.
They do not claim a failure of a correctly normalized iterated limit
along a specified nonsimplicial flag; those iterated limits can follow
different regimes and are not identified with(9) without proof.

## 7. Actual exposed faces with a closed pointed projected cone

The product coefficient also governs the following NONPRODUCT bodies.
Let K be any compact convex body in R^m times R^k, d=m+k, with an
exposed m-face

    F times{0}=K cap(R^m times{0}),

where F has positive relative m-volume. Let pi be orthogonal projection
to the last k coordinates, and assume

    Q=cone(pi K)={s q:s>=0, q in pi K}

is CLOSED and POINTED. It is automatically full dimensional, since K
has interior. Fix x in int F and v in int Q. Then for small delta>0,
(x,delta v) lies in int K, and the FULL conclusions(9),(10),(12)--(13)
hold, including L1 and first-moment convergence of the normally dilated
escorts. In particular the limit is exactly the cone coefficient(3).
Every face of a full-dimensional polytope satisfies these hypotheses:
its projected cone is finitely generated, and an exposing functional
is strictly positive on every nonzero projected generator, giving
closedness and pointedness.

Here are the local geometry and tail arguments required for this
extension. Put K_delta={(z,q):(z,delta q) in K}, and let D be the fixed
compact tangential projection of K. Always K_delta subset D times Q.

**Pointwise inner exhaustion, including cone-boundary directions.**
For any fixed q in Q, choose s>=0 and a point(a,w) in K such that
q=s w. Such an actual representation exists by the DEFINITION of
cone(pi K); closedness ensures the Q used in the cone integral is
this same cone, not just a larger closure. If q=0 use F itself.
For delta s<=1, convexity gives

    [(1-delta s)F+delta s a] times{q} subset K_delta.     (19)

Thus every compact U subset int F is contained in the tangential
section at this fixed q for sufficiently small delta. This statement
also holds when q is on the boundary of Q. A uniform threshold over
all compact sets touching that boundary is NOT assumed.

**Uniform inner exhaustion on interior product compacts.**
Let V be compact inside int Q. Choose finitely many q_1,...,q_l in
int Q whose convex hull contains V. Such a finite polytope can be
formed from small boxes covering V and lying in int Q. Apply(19) to
each q_i. For small delta their sections all contain the SAME compact
U subset int F. Convexity then gives

    U times V subset K_delta.                          (20)

Choosing U and V to be small closed balls about x and v proves a
fixed full-dimensional source ball about(x,v). This also proves that
the original proposed sources are interior for small delta. In m=0,
U is the singleton tangent point and only the normal ball is needed.

**Uniform upper tangential convergence at bounded normal range.**
For each R<infinity and epsilon>0, sufficiently small delta satisfies

 (z,q) in K_delta, |q|<=R  => dist(z,F)<epsilon.         (21)

Otherwise take delta_j->0, bounded q_j and z_j in compact D violating
this statement. A convergent subsequence of (z_j,delta_j q_j) limits
to(z,0) in K, hence z in F, a contradiction. This argument includes
all boundary directions of Q. It uses the actual face identity,
not a guessed product neighborhood of K.

Equations(19)--(21) give almost-everywhere indicator convergence

    1_(K_delta) -> 1_(F times Q)

on D times Q. The exceptional tangential boundary of F and normal
boundary of Q have measure zero in their respective dimensions;
for m=0 use counting measure and no tangential exceptional set.

The fixed source ball bounds every actual minimizing parameter.
A uniformly finite objective bound can first be obtained by taking
c=0 and b=t ell with ell in int Q*, and t>0 so small that
1-b.v>0. This denominator is positive on ALL of D times Q, and its
inverse(d+1)-st power is integrable there because d+1>k.
The optimal floor1/(d+1) passes to the limiting product along(19).
Fatou and the infinite-cylinder argument therefore put every finite
parameter cluster point in the admissible interior cone domain,
and give the same lower bound by(3) as before.

For the upper bound use the FIXED product optimum(c_*,b_*). Its base
denominator has a positive minimum on F. On bounded |q|, (21) puts
the actual tangential coordinates close to F; since b_*.q>=0 on Q,
the full denominator is then uniformly positive. On large |q|,
strict positivity of b_* on Q cap S^(k-1) dominates all bounded
tangential terms over D. Thus the product optimum is admissible on
all K_delta for small delta, with the integrable majorant

    C (1+|q|)^(-d-1) 1_D(z)1_Q(q).                      (22)

Dominated convergence gives recovery of the exact product value.
Together with the preceding Fatou argument this proves(9) and parameter
convergence(10), without an infimum/limit interchange.
Finally, convergence of the normal parameters to the interior vector
b_* and the optimal floor give the stronger escort majorant
C(1+|q|)^(-d-2). It and its first moments are integrable in k dimensions.
The argument of Section4 therefore proves the same escort recursion.

Closedness and pointedness are explicit geometric scope conditions.
A smooth exposed vertex, for example, can have a projected cone with
lineality or a nonclosed cone whose closure has lineality; the inverse
power tail used here then has no strictly positive normal direction.
This theorem makes no claim for that case or for an approach v on the
boundary of Q. Cone-boundary directions in the integration domain are
nevertheless fully controlled as in(19),(21),(22).
